header: This is how a circular's title is SHOWN on screen. DISPLAY ONLY: the title saved in the database is never changed, so nothing is lost and I can switch this off with the one constant below. Titles were typed by hand, by different people, over the years: some entirely in capitals ("CIRCULAR-HOLIDAY LIST FOR THE YEAR 2026"), some in running letters ("Circular - Selection of players for SAIL ..."), some half and half ("CIRCULAR - HTS Jan-May 2026 Session"). Shown in a list that looks untidy, so I show every title the same way: running letters, only the first letter of the first word (and of the subject that follows a "Circular -" label) in capital.

* I convert a title typed entirely in capitals. Organisation names and abbreviations stay in capitals (SAIL, DSP, PF ... see KEEP_UPPERCASE), months and a few proper names keep their capital (January, Durgapur ... see PROPER_NOUNS).
* A title that is already in running letters is left exactly as it is, except that I put right a shouted first word ("CIRCULAR - ...").
* I only ever touch the CASE of letters: every other character, and the order of the letters, stays exactly as typed (typos included).
To teach it another abbreviation or name, add it to the lists below.

symbols.name: NORMALIZE_CIRCULAR_TITLES
doc: I can switch the tidying off here (titles are then shown exactly as stored).

symbols.name: KEEP_UPPERCASE
doc: I keep these abbreviations in capitals. (Any 2-5 letter word with no vowel, like DSP, BSP, PF, HR, LMS, HTS, TT, also stays in capitals by itself.)

symbols.name: COMPOSITES
doc: Abbreviations that contain a symbol, listed apart because the symbol would split them into single letters.

symbols.name: PROPER_NOUNS
symbols.sig: const PROPER_NOUNS: ReadonlyMap<string, string> = new Map( [ "Gaurav", "Diwas", "Swarna", "Jayanti", "Mediclaim", "Durgapur", "Kolkata", "Calcutta", "Delhi", "India …
doc: I keep a capital letter on these names, in their proper form (key = lowercase).

symbols.name: CAPITALISED_ABBREVIATIONS
symbols.sig: const CAPITALISED_ABBREVIATIONS: ReadonlyMap<string, string> = new Map([ ["dr", "Dr"], ["mr", "Mr"], ["mrs", "Mrs"], ["ms", "Ms"], ["smt", "Smt"], ["ltd", "Ltd"], ["pvt", "Pvt"], [" …
doc: Abbreviations I write with a capital first letter (Dr., Rs., Ltd. ...).

symbols.name: NUMBERED_THINGS
doc: Words after which I read a lone I, V or X as a roman numeral (Part-II, Phase I).

symbols.name: LABELS
doc: A first word that is only a label of the title; I give the subject after it a capital too ("Circular - Holiday list").

symbols.name: SHOUTING_MAX_LOWER_SHARE
doc: A title with at most this share of lowercase letters counts as "typed in capitals"; this allows a unit like the km in 5km.

symbols.name: decideWord
symbols.sig: function decideWord(word: string, ctx: Context): string
doc: Here I decide the case that a single word (already uppercase or any-case) gets in the middle of a sentence.

symbols.name: convert
symbols.sig: function convert(title: string, onlyFirstWord: boolean): string

symbols.name: formatCircularTitle
symbols.sig: export function formatCircularTitle(title: string | null | undefined): string
doc: The title as it should be shown. I never change anything but the case of letters.

behaviours: empty and missing titles give an empty string
a title with no letters is left alone
spaces are kept exactly (a title is not re-spaced)
ONLY the case of letters ever changes (same letters, same order, every other character identical)
applying it twice gives the same as once (idempotent)
